en.html:
About QuotesDone

We're making UAE sourcing fair.

For too long, the best price in the UAE went to whoever knew the right person. QuotesDone replaces that with something simple and powerful: an open, anonymous market where every supplier competes — and every buyer sees the whole picture.

The concept

A new way to source — built for the UAE

QuotesDone is the UAE's first anonymous reverse-quotation marketplace. Instead of you chasing suppliers one by one, you describe what you need once — by text, a photo, a drawing or a BOQ — and our Smart Engine turns it into a clear request and sends it to matched, verified suppliers.

They compete with real prices. You compare them side by side, completely anonymously, and pay a small fee only when you choose to reveal and connect with the supplier you want. No one sees your identity — or their competitors' quotes — until that moment.

It flips the power back to the buyer, and rewards suppliers who offer genuine value rather than the best connections.

1
Describe it

Voice, photo, text or drawing — Smart Engine structures your request.

2
Smart Engine matches anonymously

Sent to verified UAE suppliers on your behalf — your identity hidden.

3
Compare real quotes

Prices side by side, shown only as Supplier A, B, C.

4
Reveal your pick

Pay a small fee only to unlock and connect with your chosen supplier.

Why it's different

The advantages

What you can't get from a phone book or a personal recommendation.

🌍

The whole market

See the full field of UAE suppliers — not one biased "I know a guy" referral.

⚖️

Everyone equal

Every supplier is treated the same. Best value wins, not the best contact.

🔒

Full anonymity

Stay invisible until you decide. No spam, no pressure, no leaked details.

⏱️

Quotes in 3–5 working days

Describe the job once and the quotes come to you — typically within 3–5 working days, with no chasing.

💸

Free to compare

Pay only to reveal. Browsing the market costs you nothing.

✨

Genuinely new

A first-of-its-kind concept in the UAE — and, we believe, beyond.

Our vision

To become the UAE's default way to source — the place every business turns to first when it needs a price, a partner, or a product. Fair, transparent, and powered by a Smart Engine.

AA
The founder
Ahmad Alzain
Founder & CEO

An engineer and procurement specialist, Ahmad has spent his career on both sides of the sourcing table. With a B.Eng in Electronics & Communication, he spent close to a decade across the UAE and wider Middle East — engineering ELV and life-safety systems for major projects, driving regional technical sales, and running end-to-end procurement: preparing BOQs and tenders, managing RFQs, and negotiating supplier contracts. Time and again, he cut project costs 12–20% with one lever — real competition.

He has also led operations for some of the region's largest events, international summits, and exhibitions — directing teams of 100+ and multi-stakeholder budgets. QuotesDone is the product of all of it: competition gets you the best price, yet sourcing is still slow, opaque, and driven by who you know. He now builds QuotesDone full-time to change that for every business in the UAE.

"I've prepared the BOQs, run the tenders, and negotiated the contracts. The best price always came from real competition — never the best contact. QuotesDone makes that competition the default for everyone."

en.title: FAQ — QuotesDone
en.html:
Frequently asked questions

Everything about how QuotesDone works — matching, fees, suppliers, customers, security and more. 150 answers, kept up to date.

About QuotesDone

What is QuotesDone?
QuotesDone is a UAE B2B anonymous quotation marketplace based in Dubai. A customer (buyer) posts what they need — by text, voice, photo or drawing — and our Smart Engine turns it into a clear, priceable brief and matches it to vetted suppliers (sellers) who submit anonymised quotes. The buyer compares the quotes and pays a 3% reveal fee on the quote they choose to unlock that seller's identity and contact details. It is operated by QuotesDone Technologies, a business licensed by the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism.
Why was QuotesDone created?
QuotesDone was created to fix how construction and services buying works in the UAE: getting several comparable quotes today means chasing suppliers one by one, sharing your contact details up front, then fielding calls and haggling — while suppliers waste time on jobs that aren't really theirs. QuotesDone lets a buyer describe a job once and receive comparable, anonymised quotes from genuinely capable suppliers, staying in control until they choose.
What problem does QuotesDone solve?
For buyers: sourcing multiple trustworthy, comparable quotes is slow and opaque, and once your number is out you get spammed and pressured. For sellers: most leads are irrelevant or already shopped around. QuotesDone solves both — the buyer posts once, Smart Engine structures the request and routes it only to suppliers who can genuinely do it, quotes come back structured, comparable and quality-checked, and everything stays anonymous with no off-platform contact until the buyer pays to reveal their chosen supplier.
Who is QuotesDone for?
Two sides. Customers (buyers) — UAE businesses and individuals who need to buy construction, fit-out, MEP and related products or services and want fast, comparable quotes without exposing themselves to spam. Suppliers (sellers) — vetted UAE contractors, fabricators, tradespeople and suppliers who want qualified, relevant job requests they can quote on.
What industries does QuotesDone support?
Construction and the built-environment services around it: building & fit-out / interior design, MEP (electrical, fire, HVAC, plumbing), aluminium & glass, joinery & custom furniture, flooring & tiling, false ceilings & gypsum, painting, waterproofing, landscaping & swimming pools, signage, CCTV & security systems, smart-home automation, solar, facilities management, cleaning, pest control, movers, AC maintenance and more — with new trades added automatically as suppliers register them.
What countries does QuotesDone operate in?
QuotesDone currently operates in the United Arab Emirates — all seven emirates — and is based in Dubai. Expansion to Saudi Arabia (KSA) is planned but not yet live.
What is the company's long-term vision?
To become the trusted procurement layer for the region — the default way buyers source and compare quotes across the GCC — expanding from the UAE into Saudi Arabia and beyond, and growing from single-job RFQs toward Smart-Engine-assisted procurement for larger, multi-trade projects.
What are the company's core values?
Anonymity & buyer control (no off-platform contact before reveal); Honesty (agents never over-promise or invent — answers are grounded in real data); Fair, quality-comparable quotes; Supplier respect (relevant matches only, seller-friendly economics); Trust & accountability (licensed entity, vetted suppliers, auditable and reversible Smart Engine).
How is QuotesDone different from competitors?
Four things: (1) Anonymity — buyers and sellers don't exchange contact details until the buyer chooses and pays to reveal, so no spam and no going around the platform. (2) Sharp Smart Engine matching — a Smart Engine reads the actual job and routes it only to suppliers who can genuinely do it, instead of blasting every lead to everyone. (3) Structured, comparable, quality-checked quotes, not messy free-text. (4) Seller-friendly economics — suppliers pay no commission on won jobs and start free; the buyer pays only on the quote they actually choose: a 3% reveal fee.
What makes QuotesDone trustworthy?
It is a licensed Dubai business (QuotesDone Technologies, licensed by the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism). Suppliers are verified before they can quote: the mandatory six are complete and the trade licence number, issuing authority and expiry are checked (see How we verify suppliers). Buyer and seller details stay masked until a paid reveal, protecting both sides. Quotes are structured and quality-gated so buyers compare like-for-like. The Smart Engine is governed and grounded — it answers from verified company and regulatory knowledge rather than guessing, sensitive actions are logged and reversible, and data is handled under UAE PDPL with security controls.

For Customers

How does QuotesDone work?
You describe what you need (words, voice, a photo or a drawing). Our Smart Engine turns it into a clear brief and matches it to vetted suppliers who can genuinely do the job; they send anonymised quotes. You compare them and, when you pick one, pay the 3% reveal fee to unlock that supplier's identity and contact details.
What happens after I submit an inquiry?
The Smart Engine structures your request and may ask a few quick questions to make it complete, then matches and invites the suppliers who can genuinely do it. You are notified as anonymised quotes come in, and you track everything in the app.
How many suppliers receive my RFQ?
Only the suppliers who can genuinely fulfil your job — usually a handful, not a mass blast. It is capped to keep quotes relevant and competition fair.
How are suppliers selected?
The Smart Engine reads your actual job and matches by real capability and location, inviting only suppliers who can truly deliver it. A wrong match is treated as worse than no match, so irrelevant suppliers are filtered out.
Can I choose which suppliers receive my inquiry?
The Smart Engine selects the right suppliers for you — this keeps the process fair, fast and fully anonymous, so you do not hand-pick from a directory.
Is my identity hidden?
Yes — completely. Suppliers never see your name, phone, email, company or exact address; only the job and general area/emirate. A drawing is shared with suppliers only after your details on it are covered (the title block, your name, phone and email). A drawing we cannot cover is not shared, and suppliers then quote on the scope and quantities.
When is my identity revealed?
Never before you choose. Your details (and the supplier's) stay hidden until you pick a quote and pay the 3% reveal fee to unlock that one supplier.
Can I cancel an inquiry?
Yes — there is a cancel button, so you can cancel an inquiry (before you reveal a supplier, at no cost — you only ever pay at the reveal step). We keep a record of cancellations, and if cancelling becomes a habit we will send you a polite, professional note explaining that repeated cancellations affect suppliers who take time to prepare quotes.
Can I edit an inquiry?
Yes — you can edit an inquiry within 24 hours of submitting it. After that window, if something important changes, please create a new inquiry so suppliers quote the correct scope.
Can I upload drawings?
Yes — you can add drawings, photos or a short video. A drawing is shared with suppliers only after your details on it are covered (the title block, your name, phone and email). A drawing we cannot cover is not shared, and suppliers then quote on the scope and quantities.
Can I upload BOQs?
Yes — you can attach a bill of quantities (BOQ), and the Smart Engine uses it to structure your request so suppliers price against your exact items.
Can I invite my own supplier?
No — customers cannot invite their own suppliers. QuotesDone sources and vets the suppliers for you, which keeps every quote anonymous, fair and quality-checked.
Can I request revisions?
There are no quote revisions. You compare the quotes as submitted; if none suit, you can decline them all at no cost and post a clearer inquiry. After you reveal your chosen supplier, you arrange any changes with them directly through the platform.
Can I reject all quotations?
Yes — you are never obliged to accept any quote. You only pay when you choose to reveal a supplier, so declining every quote costs you nothing.
Can I reopen an inquiry?
There is no reopen — simply create a new inquiry and suppliers will quote afresh.
How long does the process take?
It depends on the job, but 3-5 working days is realistic to receive quotes, and you are notified as each one arrives. Once you reveal a supplier, they have 5 working days from your payment to respond: we chase them for you after 3 working days, QuotesDone's CEO makes the final call on day 5, and if they are still silent everything you paid is refunded (banks take 7-14 working days to show it).
Can I negotiate?
Yes — once you have revealed your chosen supplier, you can discuss scope, price and timing with them directly through the platform. Before reveal, everything stays anonymous, so you simply compare the quotes as submitted.
What happens after selecting a supplier?
You pay the 3% reveal fee and that supplier's identity and contact details unlock for you. A transaction is created, the supplier is notified to respond, and you continue with them through the platform.
How do I pay?
You pay the reveal fee securely by card or Apple Pay through our checkout. It is only charged when you choose to reveal a supplier.
What are the platform fees?
As a customer you pay only when you reveal a supplier: a 3% reveal fee on the value of the quote you choose (no cap), shown in full before you pay, with no card fee on top. No VAT is charged on the reveal fee. There are no other charges to you. Suppliers pay no commission on won jobs.
Can I get a refund?
Yes, in defined cases — most notably if the supplier you revealed does not respond within 5 working days of your payment. We chase them after 3 working days with you copied; on day 5 QuotesDone's CEO makes the final call, and if the supplier is still silent everything you paid is refunded to your original payment method. Every refund is decided by QuotesDone's CEO — none is automatic — and banks take 7-14 working days to show it. Other refunds follow our Refund Policy.
What if the supplier disappears?
If a revealed supplier does not respond within 5 working days of your payment (we chase them after 3 working days, and QuotesDone's CEO makes the final call on day 5), everything you paid is refunded. That supplier then owes the exact amount refunded to you (the 3% reveal fee), the payment processor fee QuotesDone could not recover (from Supplier Agreement v14), an AED 500 administrative fee, and simple interest at 12% a year (or the maximum lawful rate) from the due date, and is blocked from new matches until it is settled.
What if I receive poor quotations?
Every quote must pass a quality bar before it reaches you, and the Smart Engine coaches suppliers to be complete and itemised. If you are still not satisfied, you can decline them all at no cost — you only pay when you choose to reveal a supplier.
What if I made a mistake?
You can edit your inquiry within 24 hours of submitting it to fix a mistake. Past that window, cancel the inquiry and create a corrected one — cancelling before reveal costs nothing.
What if my project changes?
If your project changes within 24 hours of submitting, edit the inquiry directly. Otherwise create a new inquiry with the updated scope so suppliers quote accurately. If it changes after you have revealed a supplier, arrange the changes with them directly through the platform.

For Suppliers

How do I register?
Register on the QuotesDone supplier portal: claim or create your company listing, then upload your business documents (trade licence and the others requested). The Smart Engine reviews them and, once approved, you start receiving relevant, anonymised job requests to quote on.
What documents are required?
Your valid UAE trade licence is the key document. You will also be asked for supporting details such as your VAT certificate (TRN), insurance, and your company profile or product catalogue. Keeping your licence and insurance valid keeps your account active.
How is my company verified?
Before your account is approved you complete the mandatory six — business name, mobile number, email address, trade licence, company profile and signed Supplier Agreement. Your licence is then checked: licence number, issuing authority and expiry date. We confirm your licensed legal name and trade so customers know who they are dealing with. Workmanship, solvency and insurance are not verified (an uploaded insurance policy has its expiry date tracked). The full method is at How we verify suppliers.
How long does verification take?
Verification is fast — up to a maximum of 3 working days once your documents are complete. If anything needs fixing, we tell you exactly what is required.
Why was my account rejected?
We rarely reject suppliers. You cannot finish signing up until you have uploaded the required documents on the supplier portal, so an incomplete registration simply is not completed rather than rejected. If a document is invalid or expired, we ask you to update it — fix it and you are good to go.
How are projects assigned?
The Smart Engine reads each customer job and matches it to suppliers who can genuinely do it, based on your real capabilities, for jobs anywhere in the UAE. Only genuinely-capable suppliers are invited — you will not be spammed with irrelevant jobs.
Can I decline invitations?
Yes — you are free to ignore any invitation that is not right for you; there is no penalty for not quoting. (The only charge is if a customer pays to reveal you and you then ignore them.)
How many suppliers receive the same RFQ?
Only a handful of genuinely-capable suppliers — it is capped to keep competition fair and every invite relevant, never a mass blast.
How do I submit quotations?
You quote from your supplier portal. Enter an itemised quotation — your line items with brand/model, specifications, quantities and unit prices, plus scope, lead time, validity, warranty and terms. Your quote reaches the customer anonymised; your identity stays hidden until they pay to reveal you.
What information is mandatory?
A complete, itemised quote: scope of work; line items with brand/model and specifications; quantities and unit prices; materials; lead time; validity; warranty; payment terms; and any exclusions. Quotes must meet a quality bar before they reach the customer — the Smart Engine coaches you if something important is missing.
Can I revise quotations?
Yes, before Reveal. Under Supplier Agreement §12, a quotation is valid for 30 days from submission unless you refresh or withdraw it before Reveal, and you are bound by a quotation that is revealed within that validity period. After Reveal, the contract for the work is solely between you and the customer, on terms you agree; QuotesDone is not a party to it.
Can I withdraw a quotation?
Yes — you can withdraw a quotation before a customer reveals it.
When do I know if I won?
You are notified the moment a customer pays to reveal your quote — that is your signal to respond and proceed. If the customer chooses another supplier, we let you know too, so you are never left wondering.
How are commissions calculated?
There is no commission on won jobs — you keep 100% of the job value. The only charge tied to a job is the non-response charge if you ignore a customer who paid to reveal you: the exact amount refunded to the customer (the 3% reveal fee), the payment processor fee QuotesDone could not recover (from Supplier Agreement v14), an AED 500 administrative fee, and simple interest at 12% a year (or the maximum lawful rate) from the due date.
When do I pay?
You pay nothing to quote or to win jobs. Registration is free for the first 1,000 suppliers to register, permanently. From the 1,001st registration an annual subscription of AED 1,000 applies. It is paid on the supplier portal via secure Stripe checkout.
What happens if I don't pay?
If your annual subscription (or a non-response fee) is due and left unpaid, your account is paused from receiving new matches until it is settled on the portal. We remind you first.
How is my supplier score calculated?
Your score reflects real performance: customer reviews across communication, quality, punctuality, documentation, after-sales and compliance, plus your responsiveness and dispute record. It builds a trusted reputation that customers can see.
How do I improve my ranking?
Respond quickly, submit complete well-itemised quotes, deliver well and earn strong reviews, keep your licence and documents valid, and stay compliant. Merit — not payment — drives your ranking.
Can I advertise?
There is no advertising on QuotesDone. Instead, every supplier earns a rating against QuotesDone''s standards based on real performance — you stand out by delivering well, not by paying.
Can I operate in multiple Emirates?
Yes. Every supplier on QuotesDone covers the whole UAE, so you are matched to jobs in all seven emirates for the trades and services you confirm on your verified profile.
Can I operate in multiple categories?
Yes — you can cover multiple trades/categories. Keep your capabilities profile complete and accurate so the Smart Engine matches you to the right jobs.

Requests (RFQs)

What is an RFQ?
RFQ means Request for Quotation — your job request. On QuotesDone you describe what you need (in words, voice, a photo or a drawing) and the Smart Engine turns it into one clear, structured brief that suppliers can price against.
What information is mandatory in an RFQ?
Enough for a supplier to give a firm price without contacting you: what you need, the key specifications and quantities for that type of work, the general area and emirate, and any drawings or bill of quantities you have. The exact must-have fields depend on the category, and the Smart Engine asks you for anything still missing.
How does the Smart Engine qualify an RFQ?
It reads your words, photos or drawings, structures them into a supplier-ready brief, applies the qualification playbook for that category to ask the right questions, and scores how complete the request is — only sending it out once it is ready to be priced.
What makes an RFQ complete?
It is complete when it contains everything a supplier needs to return a firm fixed price without meeting you: clear scope, the price-driving specs and quantities for that category, the area and emirate, and any needed visuals. At that point it is marked ready and goes to matched suppliers.
What happens if information is missing?
The Smart Engine asks you a few easy, tap-to-answer questions to fill the gaps. If something is genuinely unknown, it is recorded as an open item for the supplier to propose — so you are never stuck — and the request only goes out once it is complete enough to price.
Can the Smart Engine estimate budgets?
It does not invent a budget or price for you — suppliers set the price. Budget is optional. What it can show is a price-confidence band (a typical range from comparable jobs) so you can sanity-check the quotes you receive.
Can the Smart Engine estimate timelines?
It will not promise a delivery date — each supplier states their own lead time in their quote. As a rule of thumb, quotes themselves usually arrive within 3-5 working days.
Can the Smart Engine recommend specifications?
It will not push technical choices on you. Where a choice is technical, it notes it as "supplier to propose suitable options with prices." It uses category knowledge and UAE codes to make sure the brief captures what matters and to flag compliance — but the supplier proposes and prices the technical specification.
How are suppliers matched (RFQ)?
The Smart Engine shortlists suppliers by real capability and keywords, across the whole UAE, then judges each candidate on whether they can genuinely do your exact job. Only genuinely-capable suppliers are invited — a wrong match is treated as worse than no match — and the number is capped to keep it relevant.
How is RFQ quality measured?
Each request is scored for completeness against the category checklist and playbook, and must reach the "ready" bar before it is sent to suppliers. (Separately, suppliers' quotes are quality-gated too, so what you compare is complete and like-for-like.)

Quotations

What makes a good quotation?
A complete, itemised, transparently-priced quote: line items with brand/model, specifications, quantities and unit prices, plus scope, materials, lead time, validity, warranty, payment terms and any exclusions. Good quotes are easy for the customer to compare and win more often.
What fields are mandatory?
The required sections for that category — typically: scope of work; itemised line items (BOQ) with brand/model, specifications, quantities and unit prices; materials; lead time; validity; warranty; payment terms; and exclusions. A quote must include these to pass the quality bar and reach the customer.
What documents must be attached?
The itemised quote itself is what is required. You may optionally attach your own official company quotation (PDF) — the platform also generates a clean, anonymised version — and datasheets are recommended for regulated or branded items. Company documents such as your trade licence are handled once at registration, not per quote.
How are quotations compared?
Side by side and anonymised (Supplier A, B, C), all normalised against the same brief so it is like-for-like. The customer sees each quote's price, inclusions and exclusions, lead time, warranty and terms, alongside a price-confidence band to sanity-check value.
What is a BOQ?
A BOQ (Bill of Quantities) is the itemised list of materials and works — each with its quantity and unit — that a quotation is priced against. It makes quotes precise and directly comparable.
What is included in the comparison?
For each quote: the price, the line items, scope/inclusions and exclusions, lead time, validity, warranty and payment terms, plus the supplier's rating and verification status and a price-confidence band. Everything the customer needs to choose on value, not just the lowest number.
What happens if a quotation is missing information?
Quotes must pass a quality bar before the customer sees them. If something important is missing, the Smart Engine coaches the supplier to complete it, and the quote is held as a draft until it meets the standard — so customers only compare complete quotes.
Can the Smart Engine reject quotations?
It does not reject you outright — it enforces a quality standard. A quote below the required completeness score is held as a draft with specific coaching on what to add, and is released to the customer once it meets the bar. This protects everyone: customers get complete quotes, and good suppliers are not undercut by half-finished ones.
How are quotation scores calculated?
Each quote is scored on how completely it covers the category's required sections and how well it is itemised — scope, line items with brand/model and specs, quantities and unit prices, and the commercial terms. It must reach the quality threshold to be submittable to the customer.
Can suppliers revise quotations?
Yes, before Reveal. Under Supplier Agreement §12, a quotation is valid for 30 days from submission unless the supplier refreshes or withdraws it before Reveal, and the supplier is bound by a quotation that is revealed within that validity period. After Reveal, the contract for the work is solely between the supplier and the customer, on terms they agree; QuotesDone is not a party to it.

The Marketplace

How are suppliers ranked?
Nobody can pay to rank higher. A request is sent only to licence-checked suppliers for that trade, from anywhere in the UAE. Their quotes are then compared against what the customer asked for: what the price actually buys, how complete the quote is against the brief, and the delivery time, with warranty and payment terms read alongside. The strongest three are levelled into a comparison report, and every other quote is listed too, so the customer can choose any of them. A supplier’s rating on QuotesDone is used only to break a tie between otherwise comparable quotes.
How are categories managed?
QuotesDone runs a taxonomy of trades, each with its own qualification playbook. When a supplier registers a trade we do not yet have, the Smart Engine automatically provisions a new category — persona, intake questions and category knowledge — and the generated knowledge is held for review before it reaches full quality.
How are duplicate suppliers prevented?
Suppliers are matched to a single company listing keyed on their trade licence and company identity, and the directory is de-duplicated — so a company is not represented twice. Duplicate or suspicious registrations are flagged in review.
How is fraud detected?
Through automated fraud scanning and anomaly checks, contact-leak detection in the in-platform chat, decoy/canary traps, and document checks — with suspicious accounts flagged and, where warranted, blocked from matching. The anonymity model itself removes much of the incentive to game the system.
How are disputes managed?
Disputes follow a defined process: you raise the issue, it is reviewed with the full record, and it is resolved through the platform — including refunds where appropriate, which settle against the original transaction. The goal is a fair outcome for both sides.
How is supplier quality measured?
By real outcomes: multi-dimension customer reviews (communication, quality, punctuality, documentation, after-sales and compliance), the supplier's dispute record, responsiveness, and the quality of the quotes they submit — combined into a reputation score customers can see.
How are customer ratings calculated?
After a completed deal, the customer leaves a multi-dimension review, and only a customer who actually revealed and dealt with a supplier can rate them — so ratings are genuine. These reviews feed the supplier's overall reputation score.

Fees & Payments

What is the 3% fee?
The 3% fee is the customer reveal fee: 3% of the value of the quote you choose, with no cap. A customer pays it once to unlock the identity and contact details of their chosen supplier. It is the platform's main charge and it is paid by the customer — suppliers pay no commission. No card fee is added on top, and the amount is shown in full before payment. No VAT is charged on the reveal fee.
When is it charged?
Only at the reveal step — when a customer picks a quote and chooses to unlock that supplier. Nothing is charged for posting a request, receiving quotes, or comparing them; you pay only when you decide to proceed with a supplier.
How do invoices work?
When a customer pays a reveal fee, an invoice for that fee is generated automatically and available in the app. Suppliers who are liable for the annual subscription (those outside the first 1,000 registered) receive an invoice for it. All invoices are issued by QuotesDone Technologies (see the VAT note below on current tax treatment).
Which payment methods are accepted?
Payments are made securely by card or Apple Pay through our Stripe checkout — both the customer reveal fee and the supplier annual subscription.
How are VAT invoices generated?
QuotesDone Technologies is not VAT registered, so no VAT is charged on the reveal fee and invoices are issued without VAT and without a TRN.
How are refunds processed?
Refunds are returned to your original payment method through Stripe, and every one is decided by QuotesDone's CEO — none is automatic. The clearest case is a silent supplier: if the supplier you revealed does not respond within 5 working days of your payment (we chase them after 3 working days, and QuotesDone's CEO makes the final call on day 5), everything you paid is refunded. Banks usually take 7-14 working days to show the refund. Refunds for any other reason follow the Refund Policy, which recognises this one refundable circumstance.
How are commissions collected?
There are currently no commissions — suppliers keep 100% of their won jobs. The only amounts collected from suppliers are the annual subscription (AED 1,000/year, which never applies to the first 1,000 suppliers who registered) and any non-response fee, both paid on the supplier portal via Stripe. Unpaid amounts are followed up and the account is paused until they are settled.
How are overdue payments handled?
We send reminders first. If an amount due — a supplier subscription or a non-response fee — stays unpaid, the account is paused from receiving new matches until it is settled on the portal.

The Smart Engine

What does the Smart Engine do?
It runs QuotesDone end to end: it understands a customer's request and turns it into a clear brief, matches it to genuinely-capable suppliers, checks quote quality, answers questions using verified UAE knowledge, and handles routine operations — always grounded in real data, never inventing prices, brands or rules.
What decisions can the Smart Engine make?
Low-risk, reversible, well-understood ones on its own: structuring a brief, asking clarifying questions, matching and inviting suppliers, scoring RFQ and quote completeness, surfacing the applicable regulations, drafting communications, and routine housekeeping — and every action is logged.
What can't the Smart Engine decide?
Anything sensitive or irreversible is decided by QuotesDone's CEO, not by the engine that runs intake, matching and quote checks: moving or refunding money, publishing legal or contract documents, changing pricing or policy, approving high-stakes regulatory content, or anything the engine is not confident about. The engine prepares the case and a recommendation; the CEO decides, and the decision is recorded.
How accurate is the Smart Engine?
It is built for accuracy over guesswork: answers must be grounded in retrieved, verified sources (UAE codes, company knowledge), and it is benchmarked and monitored. When it is not sure, it says so or defers rather than inventing an answer. No system is perfect, which is why grounding, review and recorded decisions are built in.
Does the Smart Engine guess?
No — it is designed not to. A hard grounding rule requires answers to come from verified knowledge; if the information is not there, it asks you, records it as an open item, or escalates — rather than fabricating specifications, prices or regulations.
How does the Smart Engine use knowledge?
It retrieves from a curated knowledge base — UAE regulations and standards, category expertise, materials and company facts — and grounds its answers in those sources. The knowledge is version-controlled and reviewed before it goes live.
When does the Smart Engine escalate?
Whenever an action is sensitive, irreversible, low-confidence or outside policy — money, legal/contract publishing, pricing or policy changes, high-stakes compliance — it stops and routes it to QuotesDone's CEO for a decision, with the full context and its recommendation.
How is the Smart Engine monitored?
Every decision passes a governance gate and is written to an immutable log; sensitive actions keep a before-image so they can be undone; and health checks and automated evaluations track quality continuously, with alerts surfacing anything that needs attention.
Can the Smart Engine make mistakes?
Yes — any system can, and QuotesDone is built assuming it: grounding to reduce errors, a quality bar on quotes and RFQs, a CEO decision on anything sensitive, an immutable audit trail, and reversibility on sensitive actions — so mistakes are caught, contained and correctable.
How is the Smart Engine continuously improved?
It improves within guardrails: benchmarks and evaluations score its prompts and answers, automated evaluations monitor each agent's quality, proposed improvements are tested before going live (only non-sensitive ones auto-promote, always with rollback), and lessons from closed cases feed back into its knowledge.

Technical & Standards

What regulations apply?
It depends on the trade and emirate. The Smart Engine draws on an indexed UAE regulatory library and flags the codes relevant to your specific job — for example DEWA for electrical, Dubai Civil Defence (UAE Fire & Life Safety Code) for fire, Dubai Municipality (Al Sa'fat green building, drainage) for buildings, SIRA for security/CCTV, MoIAT/ESMA (ECAS) for products, and Trakhees/DDA inside free zones. The supplier remains responsible for code-compliant design and obtaining authority approvals.
Which standards are used?
UAE.S / GSO national standards, plus the international standards that UAE code references where they apply to the trade (for example ISO and EN, IEC / BS 7671 for wiring, ASHRAE for HVAC, NFPA for fire). The Smart Engine surfaces the standards relevant to your category rather than a single universal list.
Which manufacturers are approved?
QuotesDone does not run its own approved-manufacturer list or endorse particular companies. What matters is that the products quoted meet the required UAE approvals for the job — for example DCD-listed fire products, ESMA/ECAS-conformant regulated products, or DEWA-approved electrical equipment. The Smart Engine references recognised authority approvals; the supplier proposes compliant products.
Which brands are recommended?
QuotesDone is brand-neutral — it does not push or rank specific brands. It makes sure whatever brand is quoted meets the required specifications, standards and UAE approvals for your job; the supplier proposes the brand and you choose. This keeps the marketplace fair and unbiased.
Which materials are suitable?
It depends on the application. The Smart Engine uses its materials knowledge and category specifications to make sure your brief captures suitable material options and the things that drive their price, and notes where the supplier should propose options. It does not dictate a single material — it ensures the choice is captured and compliant.
What certifications are required?
Trade- and product-dependent: for example ECAS/EQM product conformity (MoIAT/ESMA) for regulated goods, SIRA licensing for security work, DCD approvals for fire systems, and manufacturer authorisation for certain branded equipment — alongside the supplier's own valid trade licence and insurance. The Smart Engine flags the certifications relevant to your job.
What warranties are acceptable?
There is no single fixed rule — warranty is a required field in every quote, so it is always stated and easy to compare. Typical UAE practice (such as a workmanship warranty plus the manufacturer's product warranty) is captured per category, and you decide what is acceptable for your job.
What testing is required?
It depends on the system — for example pressure testing for plumbing, insulation-resistance and earthing tests for electrical (DEWA), testing and commissioning for fire systems (DCD/NFPA), or flood tests for waterproofing. The Smart Engine makes sure testing and commissioning are captured in the scope where relevant; the supplier performs and certifies them.
What inspections are required?
Authority inspections depend on the trade — for example a Dubai Civil Defence fire inspection before occupancy, DEWA inspection and energisation for electrical, Dubai Municipality inspections for building works, and Trakhees/DDA inspections inside free zones. The Smart Engine flags the inspections relevant to your job; the supplier or consultant coordinates them.
What approvals are required?
Authority approvals depend on the work and location — DEWA (electrical/utility), Dubai Civil Defence (fire & life safety), Dubai Municipality (building, drainage, green building), SIRA (security), MoIAT/ESMA (product conformity), GCAA (near airports), Trakhees/DDA (free zones) and KHDA (schools/nurseries). The Smart Engine identifies which apply to your job; obtaining them is the supplier's or consultant's responsibility.

Documents

Which file types are accepted?
Common formats: images (JPG, PNG), PDFs, and CAD drawings (DWG, DXF — automatically converted so they can be read). You can upload photos, drawings, bills of quantities, and quotation PDFs.
Maximum file size?
There is no small size limit — you can upload large drawings and documents (up to about 1 GB). Very large files upload fastest as PDFs or the key sheets, which also gives the quickest analysis.
How are files stored?
In private, access-controlled cloud storage that is not publicly accessible. Files are served only to your own account through short-lived signed links.
How are versions managed?
Documents are version-controlled — an update creates a new version rather than overwriting the history, so there is a traceable record. Requests (RFQs) are also versioned when they change.
How are drawings handled?
When you upload a drawing, the Smart Engine reads it to draft a bill of quantities and structure your brief, and a drawing reaches suppliers only after your details on it are covered (the title block, your name, phone and email) — keeping you anonymous. A drawing we cannot cover is not shared. Your original files stay private to you.
How are PDFs analysed?
The Smart Engine extracts the content of PDFs — drawings, bills of quantities, or your own quotation — to build a clean, structured brief or quote, pulling out line items and specifications and stripping identity or prices where needed for anonymity.

Security

How is data encrypted?
Your data is encrypted in transit (every connection uses TLS/HTTPS) and at rest on our managed cloud database and storage. Card payments are handled entirely by Stripe, so payment-card details never touch our own servers.
How are documents protected?
Files such as licences, drawings and quotations are kept in private storage that is not publicly accessible. They are reached only through the app using short-lived signed links, uploads are scanned for malware, and a customer drawing is shared with suppliers only after the identifying details on it are covered; a drawing that cannot be covered is not shared.
Who can access my files?
Only you and the parties who are supposed to. The platform serves your files to your own account, and identities stay hidden between customer and supplier until a paid reveal. There is no open or public access to files — everything is served through the backend with strict authorisation.
How are permissions managed?
The database is deny-by-default — nothing is readable directly with a public key. Every read and write goes through backend functions that check who you are and what you are allowed to do (role-based access), and admin areas require additional authentication, including multi-factor authentication.

Integrations

Which payment gateways are supported?
Payments run through Stripe. It handles both money flows: the customer's reveal payment (the 3% reveal fee to unlock a supplier's contact) and the supplier's annual subscription (AED 1,000/year). Stripe events are reconciled so access is granted only on a confirmed payment. No other gateways are offered at this time.
Can suppliers integrate ERP systems?
Not at this stage. Suppliers work through the QuotesDone portal — registering, receiving matched RFQs, and submitting itemized quotes there. There is no direct ERP connector (e.g. SAP, Oracle, Odoo) today. An ERP/quote integration could be added to the roadmap if demand grows, but it is not live.
Can customers integrate procurement software?
Not currently. Customers post RFQs and receive quotes through the QuotesDone app; there is no punch-out or e-procurement connector (e.g. Ariba, Coupa, Oracle Procurement) at this time. It is a possible future addition, but not available today.
Which APIs are available?
QuotesDone runs on its own secure backend. Payments are processed by Stripe; everything else runs behind the scenes. There is no public or partner API exposed to customers or suppliers yet — all interaction is through the app and portal. A published API could be offered later if there is demand.

How Things Work

What happens if a supplier is suspended?
A suspended supplier is immediately excluded from matching — the Smart Engine routes no new RFQs to them and they cannot submit new quotes — but nothing is deleted and the reason is recorded. Suspension (matching blocked) is reversible; a full ban removes them from the marketplace. Both are oversight-first: the engine surfaces the risk and recommends, and QuotesDone's CEO decides — neither is ever applied automatically. Anything the supplier already committed to is handled case by case.
What happens if a licence expires?
Trade licences — plus insurance, ISO and manufacturer authorizations — have their expiry dates tracked continuously. As expiry nears, reminders go out and the item is flagged on the supplier's compliance scorecard. Once expired, the supplier is treated as non-compliant and held out of matching until a valid renewal is uploaded; re-verification requires current documents. It is a hold pending renewal, never an auto-deletion.
What happens if payment fails?
Money flows through Stripe. If a customer's reveal payment (the 3% fee to unlock a supplier's contact) fails, the contact simply is not revealed and they can retry — nothing is charged and no identity is exposed. If a supplier's annual subscription (AED 1,000/year) payment fails, their registration is not activated or lapses, pausing new matching until it is paid. Failed payments never silently grant access; the platform reconciles Stripe events so records stay accurate.
What happens if Smart Engine confidence is low?
Low confidence triggers caution, not action. In matching, the rule is "a wrong match is worse than no match" — if the engine is not confident a supplier truly fits, it excludes them and can return zero matches rather than guess. Elsewhere (capability write-ups, new-category knowledge, document reads) low-confidence output is marked and held for review before it is published or acted on. It escalates rather than proceeding.
What happens if an RFQ is incomplete?
The intake agent turns the customer's words and photos into a structured brief and checks completeness against the category's qualification playbook. If key details are missing, the RFQ is not marked ready and is not dispatched to suppliers — the customer is asked for the missing information (and can edit within 24 hours). It only enters matching once it is complete enough to quote accurately, protecting both sides from bad matches.
What happens if no suppliers accept?
Two cases. If the engine finds no genuinely suitable supplier, it deliberately contacts no one (never random sends) and raises an internal coverage-gap signal telling QuotesDone's CEO exactly which trade to recruit for. If suppliers were matched but none respond, response is tracked and the customer is kept informed; the request can be broadened or escalated. The customer is never handed a random or unsuitable supplier just to fill the slot.
What happens if regulations change?
UAE codes and authority requirements live in the knowledge base, and automated checks watch for stale or missing compliance content. When rules change, updated authority documents are ingested and — under the oversight-first model — approved before going live; category requirements, qualification playbooks and agent knowledge are then updated. Agents always retrieve the current requirements and point users to the official source of record, so guidance stays aligned with the latest regulations.

Policies

Supplier onboarding policy
Suppliers self-register or claim an existing listing, submit their trade licence and KYC documents, and are verified before going live (verification within a maximum of 3 working days; suppliers are not auto-approved). Approval is merit-based — there is no paid ranking or advertising. Registration is free for the first 1,000 registered suppliers, permanently; from the 1,001st registration an annual subscription of AED 1,000 applies.
Customer onboarding policy
Customers sign up with phone/email verification and accept the Terms & Conditions. Posting requests, receiving and comparing quotes is free; a customer pays only the 3% reveal fee on the quote they choose to unlock. Customers remain anonymous to suppliers until they reveal.
Document policy
Documents (licences, profiles, catalogues, drawings, quotes, signed terms) upload up to 1 GB into access-controlled storage; large files are stored in full and auto-distilled for the Smart Engine. Files open only via short-lived signed links to authorized users; parties never see each other's private documents.
Privacy policy
Customer and supplier identities stay masked (suppliers appear as A/B/C to customers; customers are anonymous to suppliers) until a paid reveal. Personal data is used only to operate the marketplace, is never sold, and is handled under UAE PDPL with least-privilege access. Data-subject access and erasure requests are supported.
Data retention policy
Operational records and documents are retained while an account is active and for as long as needed to run the marketplace and meet legal, tax and dispute obligations. Erasure requests are honored under PDPL, subject to legal holds. Agents never hard-delete data — removal is a governed action decided by QuotesDone's CEO.
Security policy
Access is deny-by-default with role-gated admin and least-privilege service access; all business logic runs server-side and secrets are never exposed. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest, documents are reached only via short-lived signed links, and posture and risk are monitored continuously by automated checks. Each party sees only their own data.
Refund policy
Refunds are returned to the customer's original payment method via Stripe, and every refund is decided by QuotesDone's CEO — none is automatic. The ladder runs from the customer's payment: if the revealed supplier has not responded by working day 3, QuotesDone chases them with the customer copied; still silent on working day 5, QuotesDone's CEO makes the final call; no response to that and everything the customer paid (the 3% reveal fee) is refunded, with banks taking 7-14 working days to show it. The non-responding supplier then owes the exact amount refunded, the payment processor fee QuotesDone could not recover (from Supplier Agreement v14), an AED 500 administrative fee, and 12% per annum simple interest (or the maximum permitted by UAE law if lower) from the due date, and is held from new matches until it is settled. Working days are Monday to Friday, UAE public holidays excluded. This is the one refundable circumstance in the Refund Policy.
Suspension policy
Suspension (matching blocked) is a reversible hold that stops new matches and quoting; a ban removes a party from the marketplace. Triggers include compliance lapses (e.g. an expired licence), repeated non-response, unpaid dues, or policy and behaviour violations. Actions are recorded with a reason and decided by QuotesDone's CEO; reinstatement follows remediation.
Commission policy
QuotesDone charges suppliers no commission on won jobs — suppliers keep 100% of the job value. The only amounts collected from suppliers are the annual subscription (AED 1,000/year, never applicable to the first 1,000 suppliers who registered, applying from the 1,001st registration onward with no fixed start date) and a non-response charge (the exact amount refunded to the customer, meaning the 3% reveal fee, the payment processor fee QuotesDone could not recover (from Supplier Agreement v14) plus an AED 500 administrative fee and 12% per annum simple interest from the due date) if a supplier ignores a customer who paid to reveal them, applied except where not permitted under UAE law. The customer separately pays a 3% reveal fee only when they choose to reveal a supplier's contact details.
Quality policy
Quotes must be itemized and detailed (no lump-sum guesses), so customers compare like-for-like and the comparison catches hidden costs, low-spec substitutions and missing items. Suppliers are vetted and rated on merit; agents are grounded in approved knowledge and continuously trained. The guiding principle throughout is accuracy over volume.

Our Vision

Why is QuotesDone building Smart Engine employees?
QuotesDone is built Smart Engine-first: rather than scaling by adding headcount, it runs on two agents. QuotesDone's CEO takes every decision that moves money or changes policy, refunds included. Customer Support answers customers and suppliers on the site and by email. The deterministic engine underneath does the routine work — intake, matching, quote checks — around the clock, grounded in verified knowledge. Anything sensitive or irreversible goes to the CEO, and every decision is recorded.
What is the long-term roadmap?
The near-term focus is depth in the UAE B2B market: sharper matching, more suppliers with rich verified capabilities, and continuously improving quote quality and comparisons. Beyond that, the direction is broader category coverage, deeper supplier and customer tooling, stronger analytics, and — as demand justifies — integrations (e.g. ERP/procurement) and possibly a partner API. Roadmap items are pursued deliberately and launched only when genuinely ready; we prefer to under-promise and over-deliver.
Will the platform expand internationally?
The immediate priority is to win the UAE market and prove the model. The platform is built to be adaptable — its knowledge base, categories and compliance rules are structured so new jurisdictions can be added — so international expansion (starting with the wider GCC) is a natural future direction once the UAE foundation is strong. It is not live yet, and any new market would launch with locally-grounded regulatory knowledge, not a copy-paste.
Will more industries be supported?
Yes — the platform is designed to grow its category coverage. When a supplier registers a trade QuotesDone has not seen, the Smart Engine can stand up a new category agent with the right qualification questions and knowledge (reviewed before that knowledge goes live), so coverage expands without losing quality. Over time this extends across more construction, fit-out, MEP, facilities and related B2B trades, and into adjacent industries as demand appears — always grounded in real, verified requirements for each field.
How will the Smart Engine continue to evolve?
The Smart Engine improves continuously and safely: agents are graded and trained on real outcomes, their knowledge is curated and kept current with the latest UAE regulations, and their prompts and models can be upgraded, reviewed and rolled back under governance. As underlying Smart Engine models improve, QuotesDone adopts them where they raise accuracy — but the oversight-first principle stays fixed: more capability, always under governance with every sensitive decision recorded, always grounded in verified knowledge rather than guesswork. The aim is a Smart Engine workforce that gets sharper over time while staying trustworthy.

الأسئلة الشائعة

كل ما يتعلق بكيفية عمل QuotesDone — المطابقة، الرسوم، المورّدين، العملاء، الأمان والمزيد. 150 إجابة، نحدّثها بانتظام.

حول QuotesDone

ما هو QuotesDone؟
QuotesDone هو سوق لعروض الأسعار مجهولة الهوية بين الشركات (B2B) في الإمارات العربية المتحدة ومقره دبي. يقوم العميل (المشتري) بنشر ما يحتاجه — عن طريق النص، الصوت، الصورة أو الرسم — ويقوم محركنا الذكي بتحويله إلى موجز واضح وقابل للتسعير ومطابقته مع مورّدين موثوقين (بائعين) يقدمون عروض أسعار مجهولة الهوية. يقوم المشتري بمقارنة العروض ويدفع رسوم كشف بنسبة 3% على العرض الذي يختاره لكشف هوية ذلك البائع وتفاصيل الاتصال الخاصة به. تشغّله QuotesDone Technologies، المرخّصة من دائرة الاقتصاد والسياحة في دبي.
لماذا تم إنشاء QuotesDone؟
تم إنشاء QuotesDone لإصلاح كيفية عمل شراء البناء والخدمات في الإمارات العربية المتحدة: الحصول على عدة عروض أسعار قابلة للمقارنة اليوم يعني ملاحقة المورّدين واحدًا تلو الآخر، ومشاركة بيانات تواصلك مسبقًا، ثم تلقي المكالمات والمساومة — بينما يضيع المورّدون الوقت في طلبات ليست لهم حقًا. يتيح QuotesDone للمشتري أن يصف طلبه مرة واحدة واستلام عروض أسعار قابلة للمقارنة ومجهولة الهوية من مورّدين قادرين حقًا، مع البقاء في السيطرة حتى يختار.
ما المشكلة التي يحلها QuotesDone؟

ما المستندات المطلوبة؟
رخصة التجارة الإماراتية السارية هي المستند الرئيسي. وسنطلب تفاصيل داعمة مثل شهادة ضريبة القيمة المضافة (TRN)، التأمين، وملف تعريف شركتك أو كتالوج المنتجات. الحفاظ على رخصتك وتأمينك ساريين يحافظ على حسابك نشطًا.

تتم المدفوعات عبر Stripe. إنها تتعامل مع كلا تدفقَي المال: مدفوعات الكشف من العميل (رسوم الكشف البالغة 3% من العرض، لفتح اتصال المورّد) واشتراك المورّد السنوي (AED 1,000/سنة). ونسوّي أحداث Stripe بحيث لا يُمنح الوصول إلا عند تأكيد الدفع. لا توجد بوابات أخرى متاحة في الوقت الحالي.

ليس في هذه المرحلة. يعمل المورّدون من خلال بوابة QuotesDone — التسجيل، استلام RFQs المتطابقة، وتقديم العروض المفصلة هناك. لا يوجد موصل ERP مباشر (مثل SAP، Oracle، Odoo) اليوم. يمكن إضافة تكامل ERP/عرض إلى خارطة الطريق إذا زادت الطلبات، لكنه غير متاح حاليًا.
هل يمكن للعملاء دمج برامج الشراء؟
ليس حاليًا. يقوم العملاء بنشر RFQs واستلام العروض من خلال تطبيق QuotesDone؛ لا يوجد موصل للشراء الإلكتروني أو الخروج (مثل Ariba، Coupa، Oracle Procurement) في الوقت الحالي. إنها إضافة محتملة في المستقبل، لكنها غير متاحة اليوم.

تعمل QuotesDone على واجهتها الخلفية الآمنة الخاصة بها. تتم معالجة المدفوعات عبر Stripe، وكل ما عدا ذلك يعمل خلف الكواليس. لا توجد واجهة برمجة تطبيقات عامة أو شريكة مكشوفة للعملاء أو المورّدين بعد — كل التفاعلات تتم من خلال التطبيق والبوابة. يمكن تقديم واجهة برمجة تطبيقات منشورة لاحقًا إذا كان هناك طلب.

ماذا يحدث إذا تم تعليق مورّد؟
يُستبعد المورّد المعلق على الفور من المطابقة — لا يوجه المحرك الذكي أي طلبات جديدة لهم ولا يمكنهم تقديم عروض جديدة — لكن لا يُحذف شيء ويُسجَّل السبب. التعليق (حظر المطابقة) قابل للتراجع؛ بينما الحظر الكامل يزيلهم من السوق. كلاهما يعتمد على الإشراف: يرصد المحرك المخاطر ويوصي، ويقرر الرئيس التنفيذي لـ QuotesDone — ولا يُطبَّق أي منهما تلقائيًا. ونعالج كل ما التزم به المورّد بالفعل حالة بحالة.
ماذا يحدث إذا انتهت صلاحية الترخيص؟
تتم متابعة تواريخ انتهاء صلاحية التراخيص التجارية — بالإضافة إلى التأمين، وشهادات ISO، وتفويضات الشركات المصنعة — بشكل مستمر. مع اقتراب انتهاء الصلاحية، نرسل تذكيرات ونضع علامة على العنصر في بطاقة تقييم الامتثال الخاصة بالمورّد. بمجرد انتهاء الصلاحية، نعامل المورّد على أنه غير متوافق ونستبعده من المطابقة حتى يرفع تجديدًا صالحًا؛ تتطلب إعادة التحقق مستندات حالية. إنها حالة انتظار حتى التجديد، وليست حذفًا تلقائيًا.
ماذا يحدث إذا فشل الدفع؟
تتدفق الأموال عبر Stripe. إذا فشل دفع الكشف عن العميل (الرسوم بنسبة 3% لفتح اتصال المورّد)، فلن تُكشف بيانات الاتصال ببساطة ويمكنهم المحاولة مرة أخرى — فلا رسوم تُفرض ولا هوية تُكشف. إذا فشل دفع اشتراك المورّد السنوي (1,000 درهم إماراتي سنويًا)، فلن يُفعَّل تسجيلهم أو سيسقط، مما يوقف المطابقة الجديدة حتى السداد. المدفوعات الفاشلة لا تمنح الوصول بصمت؛ تقوم المنصة بتسوية أحداث Stripe بحيث تبقى السجلات دقيقة.
ماذا يحدث إذا كانت ثقة المحرك الذكي منخفضة؟
يؤدي انخفاض الثقة إلى الحذر لا إلى التنفيذ. في المطابقة، القاعدة هي "المطابقة الخاطئة أسوأ من عدم المطابقة" — فإذا لم يكن المحرك واثقًا من أن المورّد مناسب حقًا، فإنه يستبعده وقد لا يعيد أي مطابقة بدلًا من التخمين. وفي مواضع أخرى (توصيف القدرات، ومعرفة الفئات الجديدة، وقراءة المستندات) تُوسَم المخرجات منخفضة الثقة وتُحتجز للمراجعة قبل نشرها أو التصرف بناءً عليها. ويُصعِّد المحرك بدلًا من المتابعة.
ماذا يحدث إذا كان طلب عرض السعر غير مكتمل؟
يحول وكيل الاستقبال كلمات العميل وصورهم إلى ملخص منظم ويتحقق من الاكتمال وفقًا لدليل تأهيل الفئة. إذا كانت التفاصيل الرئيسية مفقودة، فلن يحمل طلب عرض السعر علامة الجاهزية ولن يُرسل إلى المورّدين — يُطلب من العميل تقديم المعلومات المفقودة (ويمكنه التعديل خلال 24 ساعة). يدخل المطابقة فقط عندما يكون مكتملًا بما يكفي لتقديم عرض سعر دقيق، مما يحمي كلا الجانبين من المطابقات السيئة.
ماذا يحدث إذا لم يقبل أي مورّدين؟
حالتان. إذا لم يجد المحرك مورّدًا مناسبًا حقًا، فلن يتصل عمدًا بأحد (لا يرسل عشوائيًا أبدًا) ويرفع إشارة فجوة تغطية داخلية تُبلغ الرئيس التنفيذي لـ QuotesDone بالضبط أي نشاط يلزم استقطاب مورّدين له. إذا تم مطابقة المورّدين ولكن لم يستجب أحد، نتتبع الاستجابة ونبقي العميل على اطلاع؛ يمكن توسيع الطلب أو تصعيده. ولا نحيل العميل إلى مورّد عشوائي أو غير مناسب فقط لملء المكان.
ماذا يحدث إذا تغيرت اللوائح؟
تعيش رموز ومتطلبات السلطات في قاعدة المعرفة، وتراقب فحوص آلية محتوى الامتثال القديم أو المفقود. عندما تتغير القواعد، نستوعب مستندات السلطة المحدثة و — تحت نموذج الإشراف أولًا — نعتمدها قبل أن تصبح نشطة؛ ثم نحدّث متطلبات الفئة، وأدلة التأهيل ومعرفة الوكلاء. يسترجع الوكلاء دائمًا المتطلبات الحالية ويوجهون المستخدمين إلى المصدر الرسمي للسجل، بحيث تظل الإرشادات متوافقة مع أحدث اللوائح.

السياسات

سياسة انضمام المورّدين
يقوم المورّدون بالتسجيل الذاتي أو المطالبة بإدراج موجود، وتقديم ترخيص تجارتهم ومستندات KYC، ونتحقق منهم قبل أن يصبحوا نشطين (التحقق في غضون 3 أيام عمل كحد أقصى؛ ولا نوافق على أي مورّد تلقائيًا). الموافقة تعتمد على الجدارة — لا يوجد ترتيب مدفوع أو إعلانات. التسجيل مجاني لأول 1,000 نشاط تجاري مسجّل، إعفاءً دائمًا؛ واعتبارًا من التسجيل رقم 1,001 يُطبَّق اشتراك سنوي قدره 1,000 درهم إماراتي.
سياسة انضمام العملاء
يسجل العملاء باستخدام التحقق من الهاتف/البريد الإلكتروني ويقبلون الشروط والأحكام. نشر الطلبات، واستلام ومقارنة عروض الأسعار مجاني؛ يدفع العميل فقط رسوم الكشف بنسبة 3% على عرض السعر الذي يختار فتحه. يظل العملاء مجهولي الهوية بالنسبة للمورّدين حتى يكشفوا عن هويتهم.
سياسة المستندات
يمكن تحميل المستندات (التراخيص، الملفات الشخصية، الكتالوجات، الرسومات، عروض الأسعار، الشروط الموقعة) حتى 1 جيجابايت إلى تخزين محمي بالوصول؛ وتُخزَّن الملفات الكبيرة بالكامل وتُقطَّر تلقائيًا للمحرك الذكي. تفتح الملفات فقط عبر روابط موقعة قصيرة الأمد للمستخدمين المصرح لهم؛ لا ترى الأطراف مستندات بعضهم الخاصة.

تظل هويات العملاء والمورّدين مخفية (يظهر المورّدون كـ A/B/C للعملاء؛ العملاء مجهولو الهوية بالنسبة للمورّدين) حتى الكشف المدفوع. تُستخدم البيانات الشخصية فقط لتشغيل السوق، ولا تُباع أبدًا، ونتعامل معها وفقًا لقانون حماية البيانات في الإمارات العربية المتحدة مع وصول أقل امتياز. وندعم طلبات الوصول إلى البيانات وحذفها.

الوصول مرفوض بشكل افتراضي مع إدارة دورية للوصول الأقل امتيازًا؛ تعمل جميع منطق الأعمال على جانب الخادم ولا تُكشف الأسرار أبدًا. والبيانات مشفّرة أثناء النقل وفي حالة السكون، ولا يجري الوصول إلى المستندات إلا عبر روابط موقعة قصيرة الأمد، وتراقب فحوص آلية الوضع الأمني والمخاطر باستمرار. يرى كل طرف بياناته فقط.

ما هو خارطة الطريق على المدى الطويل؟
التركيز على المدى القريب هو العمق في سوق B2B الإماراتي: مطابقة أكثر دقة، المزيد من المورّدين ذوي القدرات الموثوقة الغنية، وتحسين مستمر في جودة عروض الأسعار والمقارنات. بعد ذلك، الاتجاه هو تغطية فئات أوسع، أدوات أعمق للمورّدين والعملاء، تحليلات أقوى، و - مع تبرير الطلب - تكاملات (مثل ERP/المشتريات) وربما واجهة برمجة تطبيقات للشركاء. ونمضي في عناصر خارطة الطريق بتأنٍّ ولا نطلقها إلا حين تكون جاهزة حقًا؛ نفضل أن نعد بأقل ونقدم أكثر.
هل ستتوسع المنصة دوليًا؟
الأولوية الفورية هي الفوز بالسوق الإماراتي وإثبات النموذج. تم بناء المنصة لتكون قابلة للتكيف - قاعدة معرفتها، والفئات، وقواعد الامتثال منظمة بحيث يمكن إضافة ولايات جديدة - لذا فإن التوسع الدولي (بدءًا من دول مجلس التعاون الخليجي الأوسع) هو اتجاه طبيعي في المستقبل بمجرد أن تكون الأساسيات في الإمارات قوية. ولم يُطلق بعد، وأي سوق جديدة ستطلق بمعرفة تنظيمية محلية، وليس مجرد نسخ ولصق.
هل ستُدعم صناعات أخرى؟
نعم - تم تصميم المنصة لتوسيع تغطية فئاتها. عندما يسجل مورّد تجارة لم ترها QuotesDone من قبل، يمكن للمحرك الذكي إنشاء وكيل فئة جديدة مع الأسئلة المؤهلة والمعرفة المناسبة (مع مراجعة تلك المعرفة قبل تفعيلها)، لذا تتوسع التغطية دون فقدان الجودة. مع مرور الوقت، يمتد هذا عبر المزيد من التجارة في البناء، والتجهيز، والميكانيكا، والكهرباء، والمرافق والتجارة ذات الصلة B2B، وإلى الصناعات المجاورة مع ظهور الطلب - دائمًا مستندة إلى متطلبات حقيقية وموثوقة لكل مجال.
كيف سيستمر المحرك الذكي في التطور؟
المحرك الذكي يتحسن باستمرار وبأمان: نقيّم الوكلاء وندرّبهم على النتائج الحقيقية، وننسّق معرفتهم ونحدّثها بأحدث اللوائح الإماراتية، ويمكن ترقية نماذجهم ومراجعتها وإعادتها تحت الحوكمة. مع تحسين نماذج المحرك الذكي الأساسية، تتبنى QuotesDone تلك النماذج حيث تزيد من الدقة - ولكن مبدأ الإشراف الأول يبقى ثابتًا: المزيد من القدرات، دائمًا تحت الحوكمة مع تسجيل كل قرار حساس، دائمًا مستندة إلى معرفة موثوقة بدلًا من التخمين. الهدف هو قوة عاملة من المحرك الذكي تصبح أكثر دقة مع مرور الوقت بينما تبقى موثوقة.

Home · How we verify suppliers

How we verify suppliers

"Verified" on QuotesDone means one precise thing. This is exactly what we check before a supplier can be matched to your request — and what we do not check.

1. The mandatory six

No supplier is matched until all six are complete:

  • Business name — the licensed legal name
  • Mobile number — verified by a one-time code
  • Email address — verified
  • Trade licence — a valid UAE trade licence, uploaded
  • Company profile — the trades and emirates it serves
  • Signed terms — the accepted Supplier Agreement
2. What is checked on the licence
  • Licence number
  • Issuing authority
  • Expiry date — an expired licence holds the supplier out of matching until a valid renewal is uploaded

These are read from the uploaded licence and checked before approval; no supplier is approved automatically.

3. How long it takes

Up to three (3) working days from complete documents. Working days are Monday to Friday, excluding UAE public holidays.

4. What we do not check
  • Workmanship or the quality of past work
  • Financial standing or solvency
  • Insurance — where a supplier uploads a policy, we track only its expiry date
  • Permits or approvals specific to your job, or whether the licence covers your specific works

Check these yourself before you sign a contract — see sections 3 and 4 of our Disclaimer. The contractual wording is clause 13 of the Supplier Agreement.

الرئيسية · كيف نتحقق من المورّدين

كيف نتحقق من المورّدين

كلمة "موثّق" على QuotesDone تعني أمرًا واحدًا محددًا. هذا بالضبط ما نتحقق منه قبل مطابقة أي مورّد مع طلبك — وما لا نتحقق منه.

1. المتطلبات الستة الإلزامية

لا يُطابَق أي مورّد قبل استكمالها جميعًا:

  • اسم النشاط التجاري — الاسم القانوني المرخّص
  • رقم الهاتف المحمول — مُتحقَّق منه برمز لمرة واحدة
  • البريد الإلكتروني — مُتحقَّق منه
  • الرخصة التجارية — رخصة تجارية إماراتية سارية مرفوعة على المنصة
  • الملف التعريفي للشركة — الأنشطة والإمارات التي يخدمها
  • الشروط الموقّعة — اتفاقية المورّد المقبولة
2. ما نتحقق منه في الرخصة
  • رقم الرخصة
  • جهة الإصدار
  • تاريخ الانتهاء — الرخصة المنتهية تُبقي المورّد خارج المطابقة حتى يرفع تجديدًا ساريًا

تُقرأ هذه البيانات من الرخصة المرفوعة ويُتحقَّق منها قبل الموافقة؛ ولا يُوافَق على أي مورّد تلقائيًا.

3. المدة

حتى ثلاثة (3) أيام عمل من اكتمال المستندات. أيام العمل من الاثنين إلى الجمعة، باستثناء العطلات الرسمية في الإمارات.

4. ما لا نتحقق منه
  • جودة التنفيذ أو جودة الأعمال السابقة
  • الوضع المالي أو الملاءة
  • التأمين — إذا رفع المورّد وثيقة تأمين، نتابع تاريخ انتهائها فقط
  • التصاريح أو الموافقات الخاصة بمشروعك، أو ما إذا كانت الرخصة تغطي أعمالك المحددة

تحقق من هذه الأمور بنفسك قبل توقيع أي عقد — راجع البندين 3 و4 من إخلاء المسؤولية. والنص التعاقدي هو البند 13 من اتفاقية المورّد.
